title: Follow a psana event
subtitle: From small-data metadata to user analysis
scope: Documents the proposed psana2-gpu implementation in PRs #136–151, inspected at e2cdad6e18fd on 2026-10-07; not necessarily the merged branch.

nodes.title: Choose a run
nodes.role: All psana ranks; setup specializes by role
nodes.serial: One process uses SerialDataSource and RunSerial.
nodes.summary: The public DataSource factory chooses the experiment/run implementation. File discovery, Configure and BeginRun establish detector metadata before steady-state event delivery.
flow: User script calls DataSource(), then ds.runs().
MPIDataSource creates role-specific run behavior; Communicators defines SMD0, EB, BD and optional small-data service ranks.
RunSerial constructs Events for CPU mode or GpuEventManager for GPU mode. Direct files, shared memory and DRP have separate paths outside this map.
nodes.ownership: The run owns configuration and calibration context. MPI CPU calibration distribution can use shared host memory; that is separate from GPU constant storage.

nodes.title: Read small data
nodes.serial: SmdReaderManager and the builder run locally; no SMD0 rank or MPI transfer.
nodes.summary: Read small-data streams and choose a coherent timestamp window. SMD carries event metadata and locations of full bigdata datagrams; full detector payloads are read later by BD.
outputs: Transition history sent to the selected EB
flow: Smd0.start() drives SmdReaderManager.chunks().
SmdReader uses ParallelReader and build_batch_view() to expose a complete timestamp window.
SMD0 tracks sent transition bytes per EB and prepends missing history before fresh chunk data. This is a send record, not a processing acknowledgment.
nodes.ownership: Reader/repack buffers own chunk bytes while transport uses them. History is maintained separately from payload reads.

nodes.title: Build aligned events
nodes.summary: Align datagrams by timestamp, apply supported selection/destination logic, and construct a coherent communication batch for a BD.
inputs: SMD stream views and catch-up transitions
flow: EventBuilderNode drives EventBuilderManager and Cython EventBuilder.
GPU split includes transitions in the CPU/SMD packet; GPUBAT1 describes L1 events and bigdata locations, not transitions.
A separate step_batch updates EB-local history. It is not a third separately transmitted transition packet. EB prepends history missing for the destination BD.
nodes.ownership: The EB owns serialized send buffers until MPI send completion. GPU descriptors refer to bigdata locations, not device allocations.
notes: The fast GPU builder appends BeginStep and then ends the batch. A trailing BeginStep after earlier L1 events is possible; see the transition walkthrough.

nodes.title: Deliver a batch
nodes.serial: No BigDataNode: local reader/builder hands batches to Events or GpuEventManager.
nodes.summary: Receive one coherent EB communication unit, unpack its CPU and GPU portions, and select the batch processor. A GPU BD is still a CPU process orchestrating reads and CUDA work.
inputs: MPI message: CPU/SMD packet + GPU packet + footer
outputs: CPU EventManager or GPU manager iteration
flow: BigDataNode.start() supplies BatchEnvelope objects to Events.
Events.__next__() calls EventManager for CPU-only processing, or GpuEventManager.process_batch(smd, gpu) for GPU processing.
BD requests further work from its EB; communication batches and execution-slot depth are different controls.
nodes.ownership: The receive/batch envelope retains serialized packet storage while managers create views from it.

nodes.title: Materialize CPU dgrams
nodes.serial: Same EventManager, reached through the local Events iterator.
nodes.summary: Decode SMD offsets, read required bigdata windows, and assemble each event’s datagrams in configured stream positions. Missing stream entries can be None.
flow: EventManager._get_offset_and_size() reads SMD bigdata descriptors.
_fill_bd_chunk() uses positional file reads for contiguous bigdata windows.
_get_next_dgrams() selects full payload or SMD-backed datagrams. GPU mode also uses this path for retained CPU and hybrid inputs.
nodes.ownership: Datagram views retain their backing Python buffers. Bigdata buffers and packet views are host storage, separate from GPU input windows and leases.

nodes.title: Plan GPU work
nodes.serial: RunSerial owns the same manager and supplies local batches.
nodes.summary: Coordinate CPU materialization, GPU read planning, byte-budget admission, execution submission and ordered event delivery. This is host orchestration, not a GPU-resident scheduler.
outputs: Read requests, task submissions and joined event envelopes
flow: process_batch() adapts MPI packets; serial iteration obtains batch dictionaries locally. Both reach _process_batch().
The manager handles transitions, splits GPU work to fit the current byte budget and issues the first subbatch read before CPU materialization.
It maps CPU envelopes and GPU event metadata by timestamp, synthesizing metadata for GPU-only events before attaching GPU state.
Slot retirement and completion tokens protect reuse. An execution slot is not an input read group.
nodes.ownership: The manager coordinates the reader, parser/input groups, execution pool, requested constants and publication staging. Yielding an event alone does not prove its asynchronous consumers finished.
notes: Current transition handling scans transitions before this packet’s L1 submission. #153 tracks ordered transition/step support.
Memory admission covers participating allocations, not arbitrary user scratch or all CUDA/KvikIO overhead.

nodes.title: Read and parse on device
nodes.role: BD host issues I/O; GPU holds input
nodes.serial: Same device input path without MPI batch transport.
nodes.summary: Use bigdata locations to issue reads into device storage, then parse XTC layout into event/field views. CUDA kernels do not open files.
inputs: Bigdata read descriptors and file mapping
outputs: InputWindow owners and parsed field locations
flow: KvikioGpuReader submits I/O from the CPU. Direct GDS versus a fallback depends on the runtime; this map does not claim GDS is active.
Optional bulk grouping coalesces compatible reads. One execution subbatch may consume multiple input groups, and one group can serve multiple executions.
The parser makes InputWindow-backed views; slot streams wait for input readiness before accessing data.
nodes.ownership: Reader/parser allocations are held by InputWindow and planned/execution/input uses. Closing a planning window and completing all dependent consumers are distinct lifetime events.

nodes.title: Run the user task
nodes.role: BD host dispatches on a slot CUDA stream
nodes.summary: An execution slot owns one CUDA stream. Prepared inputs and declared constants feed an external GpuTask callback once per nonempty selected execution subbatch.
inputs: Ready input windows and event identities
Declared task inputs and requested constants
flow: EventPool.submit() waits on input readiness and constructs BatchInputContext.
dispatch_task() invokes function(batch, stream). Inputs and outputs have a leading event-row dimension; this is not one callback per pixel.
The task owns its algorithm. Framework raw-input access and constants do not imply built-in detector calibration.
select_task_events() omits rows without GPU datagrams. Missing detector/segment policy is an explicit limitation, not assumed CPU-equivalent behavior.
nodes.ownership: Producer owners and input leases survive until registered consumer completion. Slots may overlap, but reuse waits for all relevant consumers, including escaped input-view work.
notes: Dense raw preparation is currently Jungfrau-specific; generic field selectors are separate. #170 tracks missing-input behavior discussion.

nodes.title: Supply requested constants
nodes.role: One current device copy per BD
nodes.serial: One local device copy per requested selector.
nodes.summary: Upload only constants declared by the external task and expose them through batch.calibconst(detector, key). Preserve shape and dtype.
flow: Manager setup constructs RequestedConstants and performs the initial refresh.
BeginStep dispatch updates host transition state and refreshes changed requested arrays after draining prior consumers. BeginStep does not itself fetch new values from the calibration database.
#168 proposes restoring CUDA-IPC sharing between peer BDs on the same GPU. It is not implemented at this baseline.
nodes.ownership: RequestedConstants retains host snapshots and device allocations. Replacement can need old/new overlap; escaped participating aliases retain budget charges. Cross-BD shared ownership is future design work.
notes: #153 must correct packet-relative transition ordering even though earlier in-flight work is drained.

nodes.title: Publish results to host
nodes.summary: Enqueue copies of named task publications. A copy stream waits for producer completion; one terminal completion token covers all copies for the execution.
outputs: Copy completion registered with producer lease
flow: GpuEventManager schedules PublicationD2H.enqueue() after task submission.
Bounded pinned staging enables asynchronous output copies; cap/oversize pressure can choose blocking ordinary-host copies.
evt.gpu.get(name).on_cpu waits if necessary and materializes an independent cached NumPy row. That access does not rerun the user task.
nodes.ownership: The producer lease protects source arrays through copy completion. Staging blocks cannot be reused while copies or host-result aliases still need them. Input device views use separate leases.

nodes.title: Create the public Event
nodes.serial: RunSerial uses the common Run materialization boundary.
nodes.summary: Convert an internal handoff into one public Event containing CPU datagrams and optional GPU state. CPU-only and GPU-assisted processing meet at this API boundary.
flow: CPU Run iteration handles non-L1 transitions before yielding the next Event.
Run._materialize_event() constructs Event exactly at the public boundary.
GPU manager attaches results and input state to the envelope; GPU-only metadata allows Event identity without full CPU detector payloads.
nodes.ownership: Event and GPU state retain access owners/tokens according to their APIs. Advancing the iterator is not a substitute for CUDA completion or documented input-view scope.

nodes.title: Analyze and release
nodes.role: BD user code; optional SRV output
nodes.serial: User loop runs in the single local process.
nodes.summary: User analysis consumes Events, detector methods, or named GPU task results. Optional small-data output is downstream; it is not required to create an Event.
flow: CPU example: for evt in run.events(): det.raw.raw(evt). Exact detector methods depend on the detector.
GPU publications: evt.gpu.get(name).on_cpu. Parsed input field views retain separate context-managed device access.
CPU run.steps()/step.events() expose step boundaries. Working GPU step iteration is still missing at this baseline (#153).
Use documented explicit/context-managed close for early exit; a bare break does not close a retained generator. MPI run.terminate() coordinates intentional run termination.
nodes.ownership: A scoped GPU input view must pair entry with exit so completion is recorded. User-retained independent NumPy results have their own lifetime. Teardown must respect pending reads and consumers.

edges.label: Run setup selects local SMD reader or MPI role loop.
SMD chunk and missing transition history; serial: local byte views.
Coherent CPU/SMD + optional GPU packet; serial: local batch handoff.
Events selects EventManager in CPU mode; GPU controller uses EventManager for its CPU side.
Events calls GpuEventManager.process_batch(); serial RunSerial owns the manager.
CPU envelopes; in GPU mode the manager correlates these with GPU event identity.
Joined GPU-assisted envelopes (GPU internals collapsed in overview).
Host planner issues descriptor-driven bigdata reads through KvikIO.
Input readiness and parsed-window dependencies precede slot work.
Declared device constants remain owned through task consumers.
Copy stream waits for task producer; terminal copy event protects reuse.
Timestamp-keyed host tokens attach to GPU event state via the controller.
Run yields the public Event to user analysis.

overview.title: One event, several representations
overview.note: Read left to right across the first row, then follow the CPU or GPU branch into the common Event boundary. GPU work is collapsed here.

cpu.title: CPU: offsets become datagrams
cpu.note: SMD0 and EB move small-data metadata. BD reads full payloads directly from bigdata storage and preserves transition order.

gpu.title: GPU: host orchestration, explicit lifetimes
gpu.note: Follow the middle row right to left. Constants feed the task; CPU materialization is the lower-right side lane. Input windows and execution slots have distinct lifetimes.

tour.title: Choose offline run and event T
tour.text: T denotes one L1 event timestamp, not a buffer index. Configure and BeginRun establish the context before this event enters steady-state processing.

tour.title: Locate T in small data
tour.text: SMD0 reads stream metadata containing T and its bigdata locations. Other events share the chunk. In serial execution this reader is local.

tour.title: Align streams at T
tour.text: EventBuilder gathers matching timestamp contributions. CPU mode keeps SMD descriptors; GPU mode additionally creates GPUBAT1 entries for selected inputs. A missing stream can be represented without inventing a payload.

tour.title: Assign T’s batch to a BD
tour.text: MPI sends one coherent batch to a BD. The BD is a CPU process even when it controls a GPU. Serial execution skips this transport hop.

tour.title: Materialize retained CPU inputs
tour.text: EventManager reads full CPU payloads from bigdata offsets. Hybrid detector streams can have both CPU and GPU input; an exclusive GPU detector need not have its raw payload materialized here.

tour.title: Plan an execution containing T
tour.text: The GPU controller selects complete-event execution slices under its byte budget. T belongs to an execution subbatch; that is not necessarily one EB packet or one read group. CPU-only processing goes directly to the Event boundary.

tour.title: Bring T’s GPU input into device storage
tour.text: Host-submitted KvikIO reads complete and parsing exposes fields. The input owner may serve more than one execution. A slot waits on readiness before consuming these bytes.

tour.title: Bind declared constants
tour.text: The task receives its requested per-BD device constants. Sharing them through CUDA-IPC is proposed in #168, not implemented in this baseline.

tour.title: Run the external callback
tour.text: The task sees selected rows including T and publishes named arrays. Work is enqueued on this execution slot’s stream. Completion, not callback return alone, controls downstream dependencies.

tour.title: Copy T’s published row
tour.text: The copy stream waits for the producer, then copies publication groups. HostResult retains T’s row and its completion token; copies need not be one operation per event.

tour.title: Join the event’s representations
tour.text: The manager associates CPU datagrams, GPU metadata and results by event identity. Run materializes one public Event; GPU-only metadata supplies identity when full CPU payloads are absent.

tour.title: Consume T and release safely
tour.text: User code accesses detector data or evt.gpu results. Device input views follow scoped lease rules. Slot/storage reuse waits for registered consumers; yielding the next event is not proof that T’s GPU work is finished.

granularities: Reader timestamp window sent from SMD0 to an EB.
Event-aligned CPU/SMD packet plus optional GPUBAT1 descriptors sent to one BD.
Complete-event slice admitted to one execution slot under the current byte budget.
Compatible/coalesced file ranges and their input storage; may cross execution cuts.
lifetimes: Reader/parser allocation → InputWindow → planned and input leases
Release only after planned uses and registered consumers retire.
Task owners → producer lease → D2H completion
Producer storage stays alive until every registered consumer completes.
Pinned block → HostResult tokens → independent NumPy row
Reuse staging only when copies and outstanding row tokens permit it.
Event input state → scoped view → external completion
Pair scope entry/exit; record consumer completion before slot/input reuse.

transitions.title: Transitions belong at their event positions
transitions.intro: Example: Step 1 contains L1 A and B; Step 2 begins afterward. Missing history prefixes are legitimate catch-up state. Fresh transitions keep their packet position.

cpu.label: EndStep 1
cpu.text: Finish the step; keep the run available.

cpu.label: BeginStep 2
cpu.text: Update state before the next step’s events.

gpu.label: Packet: [L1 A, L1 B, BeginStep 2]
gpu.text: Fast GPU EB can append BeginStep and then stop. A/B precede it in the CPU/SMD packet; GPUBAT1 contains L1 only.

gpu.label: Current: scan and dispatch transitions first
gpu.text: GpuEventManager._handle_steps() drains previous work and dispatches BeginStep 2 before submitting this packet’s A/B.

gpu.label: Effect: state can advance too early
gpu.text: Draining previously submitted work does not protect A/B, which have not been submitted yet. Fixed-state calculations may still work; step-dependent state is not safe to assume.

gpu.label: Proposed contract under #153
gpu.text: Preserve missing history → preceding L1 range → transition → next L1 range, with explicit state lifetimes. This is a requirement, not implemented behavior.

notes: CPU run.events() processes/swallow transitions in order; run.steps() exposes Step objects.
Current MPI GPU steps() returns immediately. Serial GPU processing consumes transitions internally, so working GPU step iteration is also missing.
SlowUpdate already reaches the host transition/envstore path; event-relative ordering still needs verification. Do not describe SlowUpdate as wholly absent.
The ClearReadout service-zero ambiguity and empty-step behavior are also tracked in #153.
BeginStep does not itself fetch calibration constants from the database. CUDA-IPC restoration (#168) must coordinate version lifetimes with transition ordering.

issues.note: P1 follow-up; current limitations, not a completed feature.

issues.note: P2 follow-up; current device copies are per BD.

issues.title: Discuss CPU-compatible missing GPU input behavior
issues.note: P2 follow-up; no-GPU rows and missing segments need an explicit contract.

serial_note: Serial offline experiment processing uses local SmdReaderManager / EventBuilder machinery. There is no SMD0 → EB → BD MPI transport. RunSerial owns Events in CPU mode or GpuEventManager in GPU mode. The shared diagram stages describe responsibilities, not extra serial processes.
